policy: CVE exceptions for the medzen-trainer image OS layer. Reviewed, expiring, and
scoped to specific CVE IDs -- NOT a raised threshold. SCAN_MAX_CRITICAL and
SCAN_MAX_HIGH remain 0, so any finding not named here fails the build.
Why exceptions are needed at all: every finding below is fix_available=false.
The perl CVE set is byte-identical between Debian 12 (perl 5.36.0-7+deb12u3)
and Debian 13 (perl 5.40.1-6), so these are unfixed UPSTREAM perl issues that
no Debian base can clear. perl-base and util-linux are Essential: yes and
cannot be removed without breaking dpkg. glibc cannot be removed at all --
PyTorch ships manylinux/glibc wheels and there are no musl builds, so Alpine
is not an option. CRITICAL=0 is therefore not currently reachable for any
PyTorch-capable base image under ECR basic scanning.
An entry stops applying the moment a fix exists: the justification is
'nothing to upgrade to', so if fixed_in_version appears, the build fails and
the image must be rebuilt rather than waived. Entries also expire, forcing
Scope: the OFFLINE TRAINING PLANE only. This image has no inbound network, is
not internet-reachable, processes only our own S3 corpus, and holds no
production credentials (the trainer role explicitly denies secretsmanager and
bedrock). It is not the basis for waiving anything in a serving image.

entries.justification: glibc is unavoidable: PyTorch publishes only manylinux/glibc wheels, so no glibc-free base can run this trainer. No fix is available in Debian 13. Reachable by every process by definition, but the container accepts no untrusted input: it reads our own corpus from S3 and a checkpoint verified by sha256 against a manifest, over no inbound network.
Same as CVE-2026-5450: glibc cannot be removed or upgraded past this finding, and the container has no untrusted input path.

REACHABLE BY OUR CODE, unlike perl: MLflow uses SQLite as its tracking backend. The database is created and written solely by our own trainer with its own run metadata (parameters, metrics, tags); no external or user-supplied data reaches it, and it is never served to a client. Moving MLflow to Postgres would remove the dependency but adds an RDS instance and rework that B5 was not designed around. Reassess at review.
Same as CVE-2026-11822: MLflow's SQLite backend, written only by our own trainer with its own metadata.

perl is NEVER INVOKED by this image. Nothing in pipeline/ or scripts/ shells out to perl; it is present only because perl-base is Essential: yes in Debian and cannot be removed without breaking dpkg. Identical CVE in Debian 12's 5.36.0 and Debian 13's 5.40.1, so unfixed upstream.
